subtitle: Lesson 1 · Noise Models in Quantum Systems

steps.label: A qubit needs isolation to hold a superposition
steps.sub: α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ only means something while nothing outside is watching

steps.label: No real qubit is ever fully isolated
steps.sub: Dilution fridges, control wiring, stray EM fields all couple in weakly

steps.label: Decoherence: the environment measures it a little at a time
steps.sub: Each tiny unintended measurement destroys a piece of the superposition

steps.label: Enough leakage collapses the qubit toward a definite 0 or 1
steps.sub: Whatever quantum advantage existed is gone

steps.label: T1: energy relaxation time
steps.sub: How long |1⟩ takes to decay back to |0⟩ by losing energy

steps.label: Tens to hundreds of microseconds, typical for superconducting qubits
steps.sub: The headline number usually quoted for a qubit technology

steps.label: T2: dephasing time
steps.sub: How long the relative phase between |0⟩ and |1⟩ survives

steps.label: T2 is always ≤ 2×T1, and often the tighter limit
steps.sub: Phase can scramble from stray fields even with no energy lost

code:

caption: Doubling the gate duration roughly doubles decoherence risk — tiny alone, but hundreds of gates compound it fast.

steps.label: NISQ: Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum
steps.sub: 'Noisy' is the central engineering fact of this era, not a hedge

steps.label: Decoherence can't be engineered away to zero
steps.sub: Physical qubits alone will always leak information over time

steps.label: Tiny per-gate probabilities compound across real circuits
steps.sub: Hundreds or thousands of gates turn 0.02% into near-certainty

steps.label: That's exactly why this course exists
steps.sub: Error correction actively detects and corrects what physics can't prevent
